page: Amazon Web Services r6a.16xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R13 processor. The instance provides 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores running at a maximum frequency of 3.6 GHz with multithreading enabled. System resources include 512 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, delivering an 8 GB per vCPU allocation. There is no local instance storage bundled with this configuration, requiring attached cloud block storage for persistence, and it includes no dedicated graphics processing units. Network connectivity operates at a baseline speed of 25 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks show substantial multi-threaded compute capability and strong in-memory throughput. The instance ranks in the upper tier for multi-core stress testing, PassMark CPU evaluation, and Clang compilation tasks. Its cryptographic pipeline, aided by hardware AES and SHA instructions, posts strong results. In-memory data manipulation is particularly efficient, achieving 68.81 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks alongside elevated PassMark database scores. In contrast, single-threaded metrics, including single-core Geekbench and sequential compression tasks, align with mid-tier results. Uncached memory read and write bandwidth tests also perform at average levels compared to smaller cached block operations.

From an operational perspective, the AMD-based hardware configuration provides strong multi-core thread density and memory capacity per allocated dollar relative to alternative architectures. However, the lack of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network volumes, which introduces external I/O considerations for write-heavy storage demands. Workloads best aligned with the r6a.16xlarge include distributed in-memory caches like Redis and Memcached, large relational and NoSQL databases, electronic design automation, batch analytics, and data pipeline aggregation.
description: Amazon Web Services r6a.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System, featuring 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor clocked at 3.6 GHz. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, it is configured with 512 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, achieving an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. It lacks integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage options, and provides a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without discrete GPUs. In benchmarking evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong multi-core processing, substantial cryptographic throughput, and top-tier in-memory key-value processing, achieving 68.81 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Conversely, single-core execution and large uncached memory throughput remain in average tiers. The platform delivers solid resource efficiency for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, making it appropriate for in-memory databases, large caching layers, data warehousing, and high-throughput real-time analytics engines.
